semantic_assessment.label_1: Consistent citation rows, plus author initials and surname abbreviations in v3; these share a baseline OpenAlex work and metadata.
semantic_assessment.label_0: A citation field was deliberately changed relative to the same OpenAlex work and metadata baseline. This does not consistently mean a different publication.
semantic_assessment.evidence_basis: Matched each error row to a none row by OpenAlex ID; compared all four metadata fields and the four citation fields. DOI, year, and author error rows retain the baseline publication metadata while one citation field changes.
semantic_assessment.training_vs_evaluation_mismatch: Training negatives include same-publication citation metadata errors; the independent evaluation label 1 means same publication even when citation metadata is wrong.
semantic_assessment.identity_caveat: An OpenAlex ID here belongs to the metadata work only. A changed citation DOI/title can identify another work; without a second resolved identifier this audit cannot prove identity for every individual erroneous citation.

notable_feature_behavior: year_match=0 for every adapter-valid year_mismatch row in both datasets.
doi_match=0 for every adapter-valid doi_mismatch row; it is also 0 when both DOI fields are empty, so doi_available must be considered.
Generic author_mismatch rows have low author_identity_score but author_conflict=1 rarely; v3 author_name_conflict rows trigger author_conflict much more often.
The given-first adapter rejects surname-only citation authors; every v3 author_surname row is skipped.
preprocessing_assessment.training_row_count_discrepancy: v3 has 5177 rows while model metadata lists 5153 training samples; no manifest or stored expected features identifies which rows were used.

limitations: No per-row expected training feature values are stored in either CSV; single/batch checks confirm only current extraction self-consistency.
The model training manifest and filtering history are unavailable; metadata training_samples cannot establish exact row membership.
The two datasets are synthetic variants and share baseline identities within each file; this is not an independent identity adjudication of every citation DOI or title.
No live identifier resolution was performed.
recommended_next_experiments: Locate the original training manifest and saved feature matrix to establish exact row membership and feature parity.
Define separate ground truths for publication identity and citation metadata correctness before any future training.
On a new held-out set, measure same-publication cases with wrong year, DOI, and author separately; do not tune on the 50-case evaluation set.
Test author_name_format and author_conflict behavior on realistic initials, surname-only citations, and incorrect names.
